stages.name: Understand the case
stages.description: Identify the objective, current situation and constraints.
sufficiency: Outcome and user defined, with a measure of success.
Initiative identified as new, migration or modernization.
Facts separated from assumptions; relevant gaps recorded.

stages.name: Compare alternatives
stages.description: Link needs to capabilities and candidate alternatives.
sufficiency: Each candidate has an associated need and supporting evidence.
Limits, dependencies and reasons for rejecting alternatives are visible.
The recommendation does not depend on an automatic answer score.

stages.name: Design the solution
stages.description: Represent components, flows, owners and decisions.
sufficiency: The diagram explains inputs, processing, consumption and security.
Region, connectivity, identity and operations are addressed.
Where applicable, current state, transition and target state are mapped to each other.

stages.name: Size and estimate
stages.description: Convert workloads and assumptions into verifiable quantities and scenarios.
sufficiency: Each quantity has a unit, period and source.
Components without a verifiable rate are shown without a price.
Target and transition costs are separate, with uncertainty visible.

stages.name: Review the proposal
stages.description: Communicate the solution, limits, estimated investment and next decision.
sufficiency: The visual summary links the objective, architecture and cost scenarios.
The advisor reviewed gaps, risks and material assumptions.
The next step, owner and acceptance criterion are explicit.

questions.text: What shape, GPU, replicas, monthly hosting hours, context and regional availability does the imported model need under the measured workload?
questions.purpose: Link the model and its test with a concrete configuration.
questions.interpretation: Validate model and service capacity requirements Do not exchange the clilling unit with an GPU Compute without checking the profile.

questions.text: What data can be entered into the model, what retention and traceability are allowed and who controls models, budgets and evaluations?
questions.purpose: Define AI's government and use limits.
questions.interpretation: To separate policies of access, data management and model appraisal assign components and liability to additional controls.

questions.text: Do we require continuity between OCI regions or selection between different models and providers and with what criteria?
questions.purpose: To clear up what decision the routing should make.
questions.interpretation: A OCI file routing for an admitted model does not amount to a multimodel or multisupplier router. design and test that component independently as necessary.

questions.text: Which prompts, API contracts, tools, context, embeddings and evaluations of the current model must preserve their behavior?
questions.purpose: To identify the change of supplier, model or modality.
questions.interpretation: To vertir the evaluation sample, compare quality and latency and anticipate rollback. changing embeddings may require re-dexing the knowledge base.
